newsitem.title: UK: Policeman shot dead in Northern Ireland bar.
newsitem.headline: Policeman shot dead in Northern Ireland bar.

text.p: An off-duty policeman was shot dead in a bar near Belfast's city centre in an attack which bore the hallmarks of a guerrilla killing, Northern Ireland police said on Saturday.
The Royal Ulster Constabulary (RUC) said two armed men entered the Parliament Bar late on Friday and singled out the man, firing a number of shots.
"We can confirm that the deceased was an off-duty police officer," a Royal Ulster Constabulary (RUC) spokesman said.
A senior police officer at the scene said earlier the attack looked like the work of guerrillas but declined to speculate which group was responsible.
Police said a burning car, similar to one seen in the vicinity of the shooting, was later found buring in the mainly Catholic Falls Road area of Belfast.
The policeman was the first member of the RUC to be murdered since the Irish Republican Army, which is fighting British rule of Northern Ireland, ended a 17-month ceasefire in February 1996.

Two soldiers have been killed in Northern Ireland by IRA guerrillas since the ceasefire ended, and a policewoman was shot and wounded on April 10. Three people have been killed by IRA bombs on the British mainland since the end of the ceasefire.

Security sources said it was possible that Friday's killing was the work of a Catholic guerrilla splinter group such as the Irish National Liberation Army (INLA) or the Continuity Army Council, both of which also aim end British rule of Northern Ireland.
The IRA's political wing, Sinn Fein, is demanding entry to peace talks on the future of Northern Ireland but the British and Irish governments say the IRA must first call a new ceasefire.
